title: Mixed portfolio — one attractive, one seductive-weak, one obviously weak
mandate: Rank three opportunities, fund the sound one(s) within the ceiling, kill the unsound ones with their specific fatal flaws, and identify the cheapest experiment that most improves the portfolio decision.

opportunities.name: RootRoster
opportunities.summary: Shift-swap + compliance-reminder tool for independent aged-care home managers.

opportunities.name: NimbusVerse
opportunities.summary: A 'metaverse for corporate offsites' with photoreal avatars.

opportunities.name: SnackDash
opportunities.summary: 15-minute grocery delivery in a single small town, solo-operated.

items: A (RootRoster): 8 of 10 aged-care managers interviewed spend 4-6 hrs/week manually reconciling shift swaps against staffing-ratio compliance rules and fear fines. 3 signed LOIs at $59/mo; compliance pain is recurring and regulated (sticky). MVP feasible in ~4 weeks; switching cost low (they use spreadsheets).
A: Risk — the compliance rules vary by region; the founder has validated one region only.

B (NimbusVerse): Big vision, striking demo. 0 companies signed. VR offsite tools have repeatedly failed on hardware friction and low repeat usage. No evidence of willingness to pay; needs heavy capital for content.

C (SnackDash): 15-minute grocery delivery has famously brutal unit economics even at metro scale; solo in one small town has no density, no margin, and the $800 covers almost nothing. 0 demand evidence beyond 'people like fast delivery'.
General: Ceiling is $800; a good discriminating experiment for A is cheap (concierge pilot in the validated region).

kills.B: Seductive-but-weak: compelling demo, zero paying/committed demand, repeated category failure on hardware friction and repeat usage, capital-hungry. Fatal flaw = no demonstrated demand + wrong capital shape.
kills.C: Obviously weak: structurally negative unit economics with no density; $800 cannot buy a test that changes that. Fatal flaw = unit economics + no demand evidence.

hidden_ground_truth.critical_unknown: Whether RootRoster's compliance value generalises beyond the single validated region (regional rule variation) — the main threat to an otherwise strong, sticky, paying opportunity.
hidden_ground_truth.good_cheap_test: Run a 3-4 week concierge pilot with the 3 LOI aged-care homes in the validated region at $59/mo, delivering shift-swap+compliance reconciliation manually; confirm paid retention and quantify time saved. Cheap, within ceiling, resolves willingness-to-pay before the build; regional generalisation is a later, separate test.
hidden_ground_truth.rationale: Tests ranking + kill accuracy + capital efficiency simultaneously: fund A (within $800, e.g. reserve for the pilot), kill B (narrative trap) and C (unit-economics trap) with correct distinct reasons. Critical unknown is A's regional generalisation, and the cheapest decisive test is the paid concierge pilot.
hidden_ground_truth.notes: Not staged. Objective checks: top-1 == A; KILL set == {B, C}; allocation ≤ $800 and concentrated on A/its pilot; B and C kill reasons are distinct (narrative/demand vs unit-economics).
